items.headline: OpenAI nears $30B funding round at $1.25T valuation led by UAE investors and Coatue
items.summary: OpenAI is reportedly close to finalizing a funding round of up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation, with UAE sovereign funds, Coatue, and BlackRock in talks to participate. The round would be one of the largest private financings ever and underscores the scale of capital still flowing into frontier AI labs.

items.headline: Anthropic revenue jumps 46% to $16.8B as it eyes record $2T IPO valuation
items.summary: Anthropic told investors its quarterly revenue rose sharply, fueling expectations of a November IPO that bankers reportedly value at up to $2 trillion. The figures highlight how fast enterprise demand for Claude models has grown even as the company posts large non-cash losses tied to its financing structure.

items.headline: Anthropic's draft S-1 shows $16.3B first-half revenue ahead of planned November IPO
items.summary: Reports on Anthropic's confidential S-1 filing show $16.3 billion in first-half 2026 revenue, with roughly a quarter of that concentrated in just two customers, as the company prepares to go public as early as November.

items.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Argon broadly to developers and enterprises
items.summary: Google expanded access to Gemini 4 Argon, its flagship reasoning model, across the Gemini API, AI Studio, and subscriber products after an initial limited rollout to cybersecurity partners. The model offers a 1M-token context window and is positioned to compete directly with OpenAI and Anthropic's top-tier offerings, though some benchmark claims have been disputed internally.

items.headline: NVIDIA expands Isaac robotics platform at GTC Berlin with new humanoid reference designs
items.summary: NVIDIA announced a major expansion of its Isaac robotics platform, including a new Isaac OS runtime, Isaac Lab 3.0 for robot learning, and open-source workflows pairing its models with Cosmos simulation. Agile Robots unveiled a humanoid reference platform, Agile ONE SN, built on Isaac GR00T and Jetson Thor, with European robotics makers including ABB, KUKA, and Universal Robots building on the open platform.

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly readying GPT-6.1 Terra, a cheaper mid-tier model
items.summary: Code changes and industry reporting point to OpenAI preparing a new mid-tier model, GPT-6.1 Terra, aimed at undercutting its own GPT-6.1 Sol on price while matching capability, as the company looks to compete more aggressively with Anthropic and Google on cost-per-token.

items.headline: Meta launches Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter open-weight model built to run on Macs
items.summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open, which it calls the most capable US open-weight model to date, developed with Apple so it can run locally across multiple M5 Ultra Mac Studios using Apple's MLX framework. The local-only design means Meta doesn't see users' prompts, and the unusual Apple-Meta collaboration surprised observers given the companies' past disputes.

items.headline: Flapping Airplanes raises $1B Series A at $6B valuation for efficient AI training
items.summary: The roughly year-old San Francisco AI lab, which focuses on training frontier models with less data and compute, closed a $1 billion round co-led by Index and Lux just nine months after a $180 million seed round — a fourfold valuation jump that signals continued investor appetite for efficiency-focused AI research bets.

items.headline: Tenstorrent raises $1.5B Series E at $6.2B valuation
items.summary: AI chip startup Tenstorrent closed a $1.5 billion Series E, underscoring continued investor interest in alternatives to Nvidia for AI training and inference hardware amid tight GPU supply.

items.headline: BIS shifts to case-by-case review for H200 and MI325X AI chip exports to China
items.summary: US export authorities reversed course on a presumption-of-denial policy, moving to case-by-case licensing for Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X chip exports to China under new volume caps and end-use certification requirements, reshaping how much AI compute Chinese firms can legally access.
